key_insight: OpenFrontiers pairs a broad corpus of open research problems with a formally checked math benchmark, revealing that closed-book rediscovery remains rare for current LLM agents.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps developers distinguish proof-generation capability from retrieval of published solutions when evaluating research-oriented AI systems.
method: Structure 12,151 research problems with statements, context, and progress.
Build a 200-problem benchmark with Lean 4 statements checked by automated probes and two independent reviews.
Grade proofs with two independent checkers in an isolated sandbox across closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions.
evidence_signal: Seven LLM agents evaluated on HQ-50 under a standardized budget achieved at most 7 of 40 resolved problems in closed-book mode; live-web success mostly reflected retrieval of published solutions.
watch_item: Live-web scores should not be interpreted as independent discovery, and benchmark results may not generalize to the broader open-problem corpus.
paper_title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
